title: Governance Principles and Procedures — company-wide policies (2027)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Governance Principles and Procedures

Short summary
This document defines the company-wide principles and operational procedures for access and permissions, change management, data classification and handling, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and the set of internal templates teams must use. It is the canonical reference for policy owners, approvers, and reviewers.

Scope
Applies to: all employees, contractors, and vendors with access to Redwood systems or customer data. Covers: corporate systems, production infrastructure, third-party services, and travel/expense processes. Does NOT replace team-level runbooks for technical operations; instead it provides the governance layer and mandatory integration points (tickets, approvals, audit evidence).

Governance principles (company-wide)
- Least privilege: Access is granted at the minimum permission level required for the task. Role-based access patterns must be used where possible.
- Separation of duties: No single individual should both request and approve a high-risk procurement, or both deploy and review their own production change.
- Auditability: All privileged operations, purchases, and vendor onboarding actions must have an auditable ticket or contract reference.
- Risk-based controls: Controls scale with data sensitivity and financial exposure. Higher sensitivity or spend requires more reviews and security evidence.
- Time-boxed approvals: Standard requests should have target SLAs (see sections below). Escalations must be documented.

Roles and ownership
- Policy owner: Finance-Legal (primary), supported by Security and People-Ops for access & data sections.
- Access owner (per system): Service owner / Product manager listed on the System Inventory.
- Change Advisory Board (CAB): cross-functional reviewers for non-standard changes; meets twice weekly for scheduled reviews.
- Procurement owner: Procurement Manager (Finance).
- Vendor risk: Security Vendor Manager (Security).
- Travel & expenses owner: People-Ops + Finance.

1) Access and permissions
Principles and role model
- Use centrally managed identity provider (IdP) and SSO for all SaaS and internal apps. Groups map to roles (e.g., role:app-developer, role:infra-operator, role:svc-admin).
- Temporary access: Requests for >8 hours must use time-bound access with automatic expiry.
- Service accounts: must be named service/<team>/<purpose> and require a documented owner, rotation plan, and no console interactive logins.

Request and approval flow
1. Requester opens an ACCESS-REQ ticket in the Access queue (Jira template: Access Request). Include: system, role, justification, duration, manager approval.
2. System owner validates least-privilege mapping and either Approves, Requests change, or Denies within 3 business days for standard requests.
3. For high-risk systems (production, customer-PHI), Security must approve within 5 business days.
4. On approval, IdP automation (AuthSync) performs group assignment; ticket closed with audit metadata.

Emergency/Break-glass process
- Use BREAKGLASS-REQ, notify oncall@redwood.com and the System owner, escalate to Security for any access that bypasses standard approvals. Post-facto review required within 48 hours.

Example IdP group mapping (YAML snippet):

# group-mapping.yaml
- group: role:app-developer
  permissions:
    - repo:read
    - infra:deploy:staging
- group: role:infra-operator
  permissions:
    - infra:deploy:prod
    - infra:monitor

CLI example to request temporary access:
$ rwdctl access request --system infra-cluster --role infra-operator --duration 8h --reason "Incident response"

2) Change management
Change types
- Standard change: low-risk, pre-authorized (examples: routine config updates with no customer impact). Target approval: automated, ≤24 hours.
- Normal change: requires CAB review; submit RFC 3 business days before planned window.
- Emergency change: bypass CAB for mitigation; document and submit post-change review within 48 hours.

Change process steps (normal change)
1. Create CHANGE-RFC ticket with: description, rollback plan, test plan, owner, change window, impacted services, runbook.
2. Automated checks: test plan verified, monitoring alerts attached, canary strategy included.
3. CAB review: meets twice weekly; approval SLA 3 business days.
4. Schedule in maintenance calendar and notify stakeholders 48 hours before.
5. Execute, monitor for 30 minutes post-change (or SLO-adjusted window).
6. Close with post-change notes and Metro-level postmortem if any incident occurred.

Rollout controls
- Canary percentage: default 5% for production deploys unless architect-approved.
- Automatic rollback triggers: error rate > 2x baseline for 10 minutes OR latency p50 increases by >300ms for 5 minutes.

3) Data classification & management
Classification levels
- Public: freely distributable.
- Internal: company-internal operational data (default).
- Confidential: limited distribution, contains proprietary business data.
- Restricted: customer PII/PHI or data covered by contract/regulation.

Storage and handling rules
- Restricted data: must be stored on encrypted volumes (server-side encryption) and require customer-data approval workflow. Access only by roles with explicit approvals and MFA.
- Backups: backups containing Restricted or Confidential data must be retained for the contractually required period and encrypted at rest.
- Logs: debug logs may contain PII—redact or disable debug in production. Retention: system logs 90 days by default, audit logs 365 days unless longer required by contract.

Data retention and deletion
- Default retention: 1 year for Internal data, 7 years for financial records, contractual retention for customer data defined per contract document.
- Data deletion: use the Data Deletion Request template; Data Custodian executes deletion and documents evidence in the DD-REQ ticket.

Data handling example (pseudocode):
POST /ingest
Headers: X-Data-Classification: restricted
Behavior: route to restricted-processing pipeline; require token with restricted_access scope.

4) Procurement and expenses
Approval matrix (typical)
- <= $2,000: Manager approval.
- $2,001–$25,000: Manager + Finance review.
- $25,001–$250,000: Procurement + Legal review + Director approval.
- > $250,000: Executive approval (CFO/CEO as applicable) and Legal + Procurement.

Purchase workflow
1. Raise PR (Purchase Request) in Procurement system with justification, budget code, and vendor details.
2. Procurement validates vendor, completes vendor onboarding checks (security, tax forms).
3. Finance issues PO and routes for signature.
4. Expenses submitted in Expensify/Concur with receipts and GL code. Cardholders must reconcile within 10 business days.

Corporate cards
- Limit: default $5,000 per month; exceptions require Director-level approval.
- Personal expenses are prohibited and must be reported and reimbursed within 5 business days.

Travel pre-approval
- All international travel requires People-Ops pre-approval and a travel health checklist. High-risk destinations require additional Security sign-off.

5) Vendor management and contracting
Onboarding checklist (minimum)
- Completed Vendor Intake form with scope and data types.
- Security questionnaire: baseline must be completed; for vendors storing customer data provide SOC2 or equivalent.
- Contract with data processing addendum (DPA) if handling personal data.
- Insurance certificate where spend or data exposure warrants it.
- Designated vendor owner within Redwood.

Risk tiers and controls
- Tier 1 (High risk): vendors that store or process Restricted data or have privileged network access. Must have SOC2 Type II or equivalently audited evidence, penetration test summary, and quarterly vulnerability reports.
- Tier 2 (Moderate): non-privileged vendors with limited data access; require security questionnaire and annual review.
- Tier 3 (Low): public tools with no access to internal systems; minimal vetting.

Renewals and termination
- Renewal review begins 90 days prior to contract end.
- Termination checklist: data export plan, certificate of destruction or evidence of data deletion, revocation of credentials, and validation that backups were removed when required.

6) Travel policy and expenses
Booking and class of travel
- Domestic flights: economy for flights <5 hours. Premium economy or business requires Director pre-approval.
- Hotels: mid-range preferred; use company-negotiated rates where available.
- Ground transport: rideshare or rental car as appropriate; choose lowest reasonable cost option.

Per-diem and receipts
- Meals: per-diem guideline $60/day domestic, $80/day international. Receipts required for individual expenses >$75.
- Receipts: all overnight travel requires itemized receipts for lodging, meals, and transport.

Expense submission
1. Submit expenses within 10 business days of return with relevant receipts and project code.
2. Policy exceptions documented and approved by manager + Finance.

Travel safety and insurance
- People-Ops publishes travel advisories and insurance details. For high-risk trips, Security will provide an itinerary review.

7) Templates, mandatory artifacts, and evidence
- Access Request template: ACCESS-REQ (Jira). Required fields: system, role, justification, manager approval, requested expiry.
- Change RFC template: CHANGE-RFC (Jira) with sections for rollback, canary, test plan, monitoring.
- Vendor Intake and Security Questionnaire: vendor-intake.xlsx (stored in Procurement drive).
- Data Deletion Request: DD-REQ (Jira).
- Purchase Request: PR-REQ (Procurement system).
- Travel Authorization: TRAVEL-AUTH (People-Ops form).

Audit & review cadence
- Quarterly: random sampling audit of access tickets and vendor renewals.
- Annually: full policy review by Finance-Legal with Security and People-Ops.
- After incidents: targeted policy or process updates within 30 days if gaps were identified.

Enforcement and exceptions
- Exceptions are allowed only via documented Exception Request (EX-REQ) with compensating controls and an expiration date. Defaults: exceptions expire within 90 days unless renewed.
- Policy violations may result in access revocation, disciplinary action, or contract termination for vendors.

Appendix: common operations snippets and examples
- Sample vendor contract clause (data processing):
"Vendor shall process personal data only on documented instructions and shall implement appropriate technical and organizational measures equivalent to industry standard controls."

- Example rollback trigger rule (Prometheus):
alert: HighErrorRate
expr: increase(http_requests_total{job="service-x",status=~"5.."}[10m]) > 100
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/service-x/rollback

Change window notification example (email template):
Subject: Planned change for service-x — 2027-02-03 02:00 UTC\Body: Summary, owner, rollback plan, impact, monitor plan, contact oncall@redwood.com.

How to raise an exception
1. Fill EX-REQ template and include risk mitigations.
2. Obtain approval from Policy Owner and respective Domain Owner.
3. Record the exception in Exceptions register (Finance-Legal maintains).

Contact and escalation
- Policy owner: policies@redwood.com (Finance-Legal)
- Security vendor manager: vendor-risk@redwood.com
- Access & IdP team: idp-ops@redwood.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Travel & People Ops: travel@redwood.com

Revision history
- 2026-08-01: Initial company-wide consolidation (created).
- 2026-12-10: Add vendor tiering and renewal window updates.
- 2027-01-12: Finalized travel pre-approval workflow and emergency access post-facto review SLA.

This document should be used as the authoritative starting point; teams must link their team-level process pages to this page and attach required artifacts (tickets, contracts) to provide audit evidence.
